questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. Cheetahs are one of the world's most-recognisable cats, known especially for their speed.

B. Their faces too are distinguished by prominent black lines that curve from the inner corner of each eye to the outer corners of the mouth, like a well-worn trail of inky tears.

C. Cheetahs are covered almost entirely with small black spots on a background of pale yellow and have a white underbelly.

D. They have a long, slender body measuring 1.2 metres (4 feet), with a long tail (65-85 cm [2-3 feet]) that generally ends in a white tuft.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'ABDC'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
 
• We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'. 
 
• Here, **'Sentence A'** should be the first sentence because the given paragraph is talking about the Cheetas. And **Sentence A **is an introductory sentence.
 
• **Sentence B** will be the next sentence. (Moreover, only **option 1** starts with **'A',** therefore we can instantly mark it as the correct answer)
 
• **Sentence B** is talking about the physical appearance of '**Cheetahs**' and** Sentence D** is also talking about the physical appearance. Hence, both of these sentences are connected.
 
• **Hence, sentence D** will be the next sentence.
 
• Lastly, **Sentence C** will be used.
 
• Thus, the correct sequence is:
 
 
• **A**: Cheetahs are one of the world's most-recognisable cats, known especially for their speed.
 
• **B**: Their faces too are distinguished by prominent black lines that curve from the inner corner of each eye to the outer corners of the mouth, like a well-worn trail of inky tears.
 
• **D**: They have a long, slender body measuring 1.2 metres (4 feet), with a long tail (65-85 cm [2-3 feet]) that generally ends in a white tuft.
 
• **C**: Cheetahs are covered almost entirely with small black spots on a background of pale yellow and have a white underbelly.

 
 
 

**Correct Sequence:__** *Cheetahs are one of the world's most-recognisable cats, known especially for their speed. Their faces too are distinguished by prominent black lines that curve from the inner corner of each eye to the outer corners of the mouth, like a well-worn trail of inky tears. They have a long, slender body measuring 1.2 metres (4 feet), with a long tail (65-85 cm [2-3 feet]) that generally ends in a white tuft. Cheetahs are covered almost entirely with small black spots on a background of pale yellow and have a white underbelly.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, Select 'No substitution required'.**

The roof __**is being held up over**__ two stone pillars.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'is held up by'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here, **'is held up by'** should be used instead of** 'is being held up over'.**
 
• **By **is used to show the person or thing that does something.
 
 
• For Example - I felt frightened **by **the anger in his voice.
 
 
 
• **Hold up** is a **phrasal verb** meaning **support and prevent something from falling.**
 
 
• For Example - Concrete pillars **hold up** the elevated section of the railway.
 
 
 
• The use of 'Being' is wrong because it is used in the present or past continuous tense.
 
• **'Being'** is used in the passive sense and it is wrong in the context of the given sentence.

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *The roof **is held up by **two stone pillars.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__**

__
 
• दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है।
 
• यहाँ, **'**is held up by**' **का प्रयोग** '**is being held up over**' **के स्थान पर किया जाना चाहिए।
 
• **By **का उपयोग उस व्यक्ति या चीज़ को दिखाने के लिए किया जाता है जो कुछ करता है।
 
 
• उदाहरण के लिए - I felt frightened by the anger in his voice.
 
 
 
• Hold up एक वाक्यांश क्रिया है जिसका अर्थ है **समर्थन करना और किसी चीज को गिरने से रोकना**।
 
 
• उदाहरण के लिए - Concrete pillars hold up the elevated section of the railway.
 
 
 
• '**Being**' का प्रयोग गलत है क्योंकि इसका प्रयोग **present or past continuous tense** में होता है।
 
• '**Being**' का प्रयोग **passive sense** में किया गया है और यह दिए गए वाक्य के संदर्भ में गलत है।

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

At the last moment, a fireman pulled out Manohar from the burning bus.

options.text: At the last moment, Manohar had been pulled out of the burning bus by a fireman.
At the last moment, Manohar was pulled out of the burning bus by a fireman.
At the last moment, a fireman was pulled out of the burning bus by Manohar.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'At the last moment, Manohar was pulled out of the burning bus by a fireman.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Active Voice. As per the given question, we have to change it into Passive Voice. 
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• Subject + V2 + Object. (Active Voice)
 
• Subject (objective case) + was/were + V3 + Object (subjective case). (Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• *Example:*
 
 
• *Their cousin **showed **them some rare photographs. (Active Voice)*
 
• *They **were shown** some rare photographs by their cousin. (Passive Voice)*
 
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is 'A fireman'.​​
 
• The object of the given sentence is 'Manohar'. 
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject.
 
• And 'pulled' will be changed into 'was pulled'. 
 
• Lastly, the preposition 'by' will be added. 

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *At the last moment, Manohar was pulled out of the burning bus by a fireman.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__**

 
• ​दिया गया वाक्य Active Voice में है। दिए गए प्रश्न के अनुसार हमें इसे Passive Voice में बदलना है।
 
• दिए गए वाक्य की संरचना इस प्रकार है:
 
 
• Subject + V2 + Object. (Active Voice)
 
• Subject (objective case) + was/were + V3 + Object (subjective case). (Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• उदाहरण:
 
 
• *Their cousin **showed **them some rare photographs. (Active Voice)*
 
• *They **were shown** some rare photographs by their cousin. (Passive Voice)*
 
 
 
• दिए गए वाक्य का subject 'A fireman' है।​
 
• दिए गए वाक्य का object 'Manohar' है।
 
• Object के स्थान पर Subject रखा जाएगा और Subject के स्थान पर Object रखा जाएगा।
 
• 'pulled' को 'was pulled' में बदल दिया जाएगा।
 
• अंत में, preposition 'by' जोड़ा जाएगा।

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.**

A. He confessed that the only thing he was afraid of was snakes.

B. On my second visit to West Africa, I met a young man on board the ship.

C. I told him that it was very unlikely that he would see any.

D. He was going out to take up a job in a banana plantation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**BDAC**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
 
• We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'. 
 
• Here, **Sentence B** will be the first sentence because it is the starting of an incident i.e. the narrator meeting a young man on the ship.
 
• **Sentence B** is talking about a young man and **Sentence D** is further explaining why the young man was going out.
 
• **Sentence A** will be the next sentence because it is talking about what the young man confessed to the narrator.
 
• Lastly, **Sentence C** will be used because it is talking about what the narrator replied to the young man.
 
• Thus, the correct sequence is:
 
 
• **B**: On my second visit to West Africa, I met a young man on board the ship.
 
• **D**: He was going out to take up a job in a banana plantation.
 
• **A**: He confessed that the only thing he was afraid of was snakes.
 
• **C**: I told him that it was very unlikely that he would see any.

 
 
 

**Correct Sequence:__** *On my second visit to West Africa, I met a young man on board the ship. He was going out to take up a job in a banana plantation. He confessed that the only thing he was afraid of was snakes. I told him that it was very unlikely that he would see any.*
